edges.description: Reproduces the essential genetic logic of the human disease: complete Mcm4 loss is preimplantation-lethal, and only a hypomorphic allele is compatible with development. That is the reason the human disorder exists as a viable syndrome at all.
edges.limitations: The mechanism of hypomorphism differs from the human one. Chaos3 is a destabilizing missense substitution; the human allele is a frameshift rescued by downstream translation re-initiation into a shorter isoform. The mouse therefore models residual-activity biology but not the isoform switch, and cannot be used to reason about which MCM4 domains the patients retain.

edges.limitations: The mouse develops mammary adenocarcinoma in over 80% of homozygous females, an outcome with no counterpart yet reported in a human patient. Reading that across would overstate what is known about cancer risk in NKGCD; see the knowledge gap attached to this node.

nodes.description: Most licensed origins are never used. They exist as a reserve that fires when a replication fork stalls, and that reserve is the first line of defence for the genome. Reduced MCM2-7 leaves fewer of them, which is the specific reason a partial licensing defect produces instability rather than simply slower replication.

evidence.reference_title: How dormant origins promote complete genome replication.
evidence.snippet: Mice expressing reduced levels of MCM2-7 have fewer dormant origins, are cancer-prone and are genetically unstable, demonstrating the importance of dormant origins for preserving genome integrity.

evidence.reference_title: Role of DNA damage response pathways in preventing carcinogenesis caused by intrinsic replication stress.
evidence.snippet: we utilized the Mcm4(Chaos3/Chaos3) ('Chaos3') mouse model that, by virtue of an amino-acid alteration in MCM4 that destabilizes the MCM2-7 DNA replicative helicase, has fewer dormant replication origins and an increased number of stalled replication forks. This leads to genomic instability and cancer in most Chaos3 mice.

nodes.description: Reported once, in the index case P1.3, who developed an EBV-driven lymphoproliferative disorder of the small bowel at two years and nine months; the tumour was resected. One case in six reported patients supports the phenotype and no risk estimate, which is why the cancer-risk knowledge gap stands alongside it.

nodes.description: The selective part of the phenotype, and the part that explains why a housekeeping defect produces an immunodeficiency. Terminal maturation from CD56-bright to CD56-dim is tightly dependent on MCM4-dependent cell division, so the compartment that needs the most divisions is the one that fails. Independent work shows CD56-bright NK cells accumulate more DNA damage and replication stress on activation than either CD56-dim NK cells or T cells, and die by apoptosis under aphidicolin, which supplies the cell-intrinsic reason for the selectivity.

nodes.description: In Mcm4-depleted mice the adrenal cortex is grossly abnormal: non-steroidogenic GATA4- and Gli1-positive cells appear within the steroidogenic cortex and the number of steroidogenic cells in the zona fasciculata falls. That is a structural account of the glucocorticoid deficiency rather than a functional one, and it is what distinguishes this adrenal failure from the ACTH-receptor and redox lesions of the classic FGD series.

nodes.description: A forward-genetic chromosome-instability mutant that turned out to be a viable hypomorphic Mcm4 allele. It is the closest available model of the human lesion in kind rather than in sequence: an amino acid change destabilizing MCM4, on a background where the disrupted allele is preimplantation-lethal.

ACTH-resistant glucocorticoid deficiency, presenting later than in the classic FGD series. The founding cohort describes the symptomatic presentation as delayed in onset and possibly a secondary phenotype. The band is VERY_FREQUENT rather than OBLIGATE because that same cohort names a member who lacked it. Counting from the founding report: kindred A has five affected children, and adrenal insufficiency requiring replacement developed in four of them, the index case P1.3 plus P1.2, P1.4 and P1.5. The unrelated patient P2.1 in kindred B was also diagnosed with it, so it is five of the six reported patients, with P1.1 the only exception. Whether that reflects incomplete penetrance or an onset later than the age at report is not something any cited source settles, so the band records the observed fraction rather than either explanation.
